name: Ex-situ mineral carbonation
principle: Crushed Mg/Ca silicates or alkaline wastes react with CO2 in a plant to form stable carbonates. The ECN review found direct aqueous carbonation the most promising route (olivine 91% in 6 h at about 185 degC and 150 atm), with an energy penalty of about 27% of a power plant (75% from grinding) and best-case costs of EUR 42/t CO2 for olivine, 49 for wollastonite and 78 for serpentine.

performance.metric: olivine conversion in direct aqueous route
performance.basis: 6 h, about 185 degC, about 150 atm CO2, feed 80% below 37 um

source.note: ECN/TNO review of mineral carbonation routes (2003-2004 literature)
